objective: Construct explicit pattern-sensitive partitions, crossing-edit tolerance, and same-order split domination certificates for a nonsplit chordal block family.

atomic_claims.text: Cyclic triangle lifts and odd-modulus K4 lifts partition all intergroup links; one-point padding handles every even group size.
The four-block split family on n=8q vertices has cp<=(11/128)n^2+(7/16)n+2 by three triangle motifs, one K4 motif and residual J(q,q) partitions.
With a p_F-piece partition of the outside graph, D crossing deletions and A crossing additions raise the displayed bound by at most p_F+2D+A.
Replacing each outside block by a clique yields a nonsplit chordal family for q>=2 with delta=2q(q-1) and cp<=floor(8q(8q+1)/6).

assumptions: Finite simple graphs; exact edge partitions.
Four core blocks and four outside blocks each have q vertices, with the specified initial crossing pattern.
C01 matching partition and attained benchmark are candidate proof inputs.
For general outside edges their partition size p_F must be supplied.
risks: No mathematical execution, optimality certificate or verifier receipt.
Only explicit block templates and the stated edit neighborhood are covered; no universal reduction is assumed.
Odd moduli need not be prime, but the four-coordinate construction must not be used unpadded at an even modulus.
The edit bound is specific to small mixed pieces and crossing edits, not a Lipschitz theorem for general cp.
